supporting_observations.claim: On WS-ICHEN-01, ivy.chen opened Statement.docm in Word shortly before Word launched PowerShell as a child process.

The PowerShell command used hidden-window and no-profile options with an encoded command. Decoding the command indicates it downloads and executes a script from raw.githubusercontent.com/nwd-it/tools/main/u.ps1.
Proxy evidence records a successful request for that same u.ps1 URL, consistent with the PowerShell download command.
The PowerShell process launched rundll32 to invoke Init in C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll; the recorded process exited shortly afterward.
The Word-to-hidden-PowerShell download-and-execute sequence, followed by execution of a DLL from the user's Roaming profile, supports a malicious-activity finding for the alerted activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: The stated winsec and Sysmon collection outage applies to WS-NBLAKE-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC; it does not list WS-ICHEN-01 as affected.
The supplied evidence records the PowerShell command and requested script URL, but does not include the downloaded script body or the contents, hash, or signature of svchelper.dll.
The help desk report gives an approximate time of 13:40 UTC; the observed Word and PowerShell activity begins at 13:41:50 UTC.
claims_not_established: What the downloaded script or svchelper.dll does beyond the recorded invocation.
Whether the activity established persistence, accessed or exfiltrated data, or affected other systems.
How Statement.docm arrived on the workstation or whether ivy.chen knowingly opened it.
Whether the GitHub repository or its contents are controlled by an authorized organization.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and analyze Statement.docm, the downloaded u.ps1 content, and svchelper.dll; preserve hashes and relevant file metadata.
Collect available endpoint investigation data for WS-ICHEN-01, including file creation, script-block or AMSI logs, persistence changes, and subsequent network activity.
Review the document's origin and delivery path, and determine whether similar document, script, or DLL activity occurred on other hosts.
unrelated_findings: Separate review: WS-ICHEN-01 appears to have obtained a Kerberos ticket for sam.okafor targeting WS-SOKAFOR-01, followed by a network logon for sam.okafor on WS-SOKAFOR-01 originating from WS-ICHEN-01. Inventory context says remote administration is only done from WS-SOKAFOR-01; the records do not establish what action, if any, followed this logon. This is not used to decide the alerted activity. (T043-00080, T043-00082, T043-00084)
